title: Steady headroom shaper and eviction policy for tenant throughput guarantees
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Implement a tenant-aware admission controller for Dedicated fleets that enforces steady throughput guarantees while preserving headroom for latency SLOs and enabling graceful overload shedding. This ticket covers the shaper algorithm, eviction/penalty rules, instrumentation, and a staged rollout.

Problem context:
- Customers on Dedicated pools require throughput guarantees and predictable tail latency. When demand spikes, naive rate limiting either starves high-priority tenants or causes large latency spikes before autoscale reacts.
- Current admission components don't jointly consider queueing headroom, autoscaler signals, and cache eviction for KV/prefix caches. We need a unified control that preserves SLAs and gives autoscaler useful signals.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Steady Headroom Shaper
- Per-tenant token-bucket with two tokens: steady_rate and burst_capacity. steady_rate maps to the committed throughput tier; burst_capacity is bounded by configured headroom and decays continuously.
- A global queue depth budget (per-pool) reserves N slots for latency-sensitive requests. Admission checks estimate on-deck latency using current in-flight tokens and average per-token service time.
- Shaper exposes metrics: tenant_allowed_rps, tenant_rejected_rps, estimated_on_deck_ms.

2) Queueing + Dynamic Timeouts
- Requests that cannot immediately pass the token-bucket enter a short-priority queue with a dynamic timeout computed from remaining headroom and target p95 latency. If a request times out in queue, it is classified as failed-by-shedder (for metrics & billing decisions).

3) Overload Shedding / Eviction Policy
- Implement multi-factor eviction when queue/backpressure crosses thresholds:
  - First: soft-shed lower-priority background jobs (labels: batch/async)
  - Second: throttle burst tokens for tenants exceeding their moving-window usage
  - Third: reject new requests from tenants that have been penalized frequently (exponential backoff)
- Eviction of prefix/KV caches for tenants that are currently rate-limited: prefer evicting largest, least-recently-used entries to reclaim memory for healthy tenants. This helps avoid tail latency amplification under memory pressure.

4) Autoscaler integration
- Emit signals: sustained_queue_depth, headroom_utilization, rejected_rps_by_tenant. Make these available to Dedicated autoscaler as short-lived metrics for faster scaling decisions (target: reduce median scale reaction from 90s -> 30s).
- Provide optional policy that triggers proactive scale-up when headroom_utilization > 70% for X seconds.

5) Fairness & Isolation
- Implement weighted-leasing to ensure tenants with higher committed throughput still yield to safety policies but retain priority over free-tier traffic.

Instrumentation and observability:
- New metrics (tenant_allowed_rps, tenant_rejected_rps, queue_timeout_count, shedder_eviction_count, headroom_utilization) and per-tenant traces for admission decisions.
- Dashboard: Dedicated -> Pool X -> Admission Control view showing headroom, queue lengths, top rejected tenants, autoscale triggers.

Testing & QA:
- Unit tests for token-bucket math and dynamic timeout heuristics.
- Integration tests using load generator (github.com/redwood-inference/loadbench) with synthetic tenants exercising burst and steady patterns.
- Chaos test: induce node slowdowns and memory pressure to exercise eviction path.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0: Feature flagged in non-prod with metrics only (no rejection) for 1 week.
- Phase 1: Canary 5% traffic on a single Dedicated pool with soft-shedding enabled for background jobs.
- Phase 2: 25% traffic with full shaper enabled and auto-unlock for false positives.
- Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 100% with monitoring runbook and rollback to current admission behavior.

Acceptance criteria:
- Admission controller enforces per-tenant steady_rate within +/- 10% under normal load.
- p95 latency does not regress beyond configured SLO when headroom_utilization <= 70%.
- Autoscaler receives headroom signals and demonstrates improved scale-up responsiveness in synthetic test (median from 90s -> <=35s).
- No data plane errors or request correctness regressions in canary.

Open decisions / trade-offs:
- Token-bucket vs leaky-bucket: token-bucket chosen for simplicity and existing metrics compatibility; may revisit if fairness anomalies appear.
- Whether eviction should be tenant-global or pool-global; current design does tenant-local eviction with pool-level limits to avoid starving small tenants in multi-tenant pools.
- Billing implications for rejected/shed requests (charging or not) must be confirmed with finance - created ENG-18550-finance-shedder-billing to coordinate.
